title: Register to vote or update a registration
question: How do I register to vote in Albemarle County or change my address?
office: Albemarle County Voter Registration and Elections (the General Registrar's office; the County also calls it the Office of Elections). The General Registrar is appointed by the Albemarle County Electoral Board.
summary: Albemarle County's Voter Registration and Elections office (the General Registrar) registers county residents under state law. With a Virginia driver's license or DMV ID you can register or update your address or name online on the Department of Elections Citizen Portal. Otherwise mail the state VA-NVRA-1 form, postmarked by the deadline, or apply in person at the County Office Building, 1600 5th Street. October 23, 2026 is the last day of regular registration for the November 3, 2026 election; the records are then closed for the 10 days before it. From October 24 through Election Day you can still register in person, at the office during early voting or at your polling place, and vote a provisional ballot. A denial can be appealed to the Albemarle Circuit Court within 10 days of being notified of it ($10 fee).

steps.step: Check that you are eligible to register in Albemarle County
steps.how: You must be a U.S. citizen and a resident of Virginia and of Albemarle County: state law requires both domicile (you live here and intend to stay) and a place of abode here. A home split by the city-county line counts where your bedroom is. You must be at least 18 by the next November general election. The County also lists that you must not be registered or planning to vote in another state, or currently declared mentally incompetent by a court. Felony convictions: the County says the conviction must not be for a felony recognized at common law in 1870, and that anyone convicted of such a felony must have the right to vote restored. The Department of Elections says that, under a 2026 federal court order, only those felonies take away the right to vote (it lists Va. Code §§ 18.2-32, 18.2-35 and 18.2-36), and that other felons may register once released. It also says no one may register while physically incarcerated for a felony; such an application is held until release. Va. Code § 24.2-101 as indexed still states the older rule (see caveats). Students may register at their campus address.

steps.step: Confirm you live in the county, not the City of Charlottesville, and check whether you are already registered
steps.who: Applicant; Virginia Department of Elections (Citizen Portal); Voter Registration and Elections office
steps.how: Look up your record on the Department of Elections Citizen Portal, or ask the county office (434-972-4173 or VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org). Make sure your home address is in Albemarle County. Charlottesville is a separate independent city with its own registrar, and its own registration page warns that the city and county borders are confusing. If a lookup finds no record, try the other locality and then your previous Virginia locality. Albemarle has 30 precincts, including a University precinct (No. 202, voting at the Slaughter Recreation Center). Your precinct and polling place follow from the home address you register.

steps.step: Register or update online through the Citizen Portal
steps.who: Applicant with a Virginia driver's license or DMV-issued ID card
steps.how: Complete the electronic application on the Department of Elections Citizen Portal. Your Social Security number and DMV customer number must match DMV records, and DMV's copy of your signature is used. The Department of Elections sends the completed application to the Albemarle registrar within five business days. Without a DMV credential, use the paper form (step s4).
steps.deadline: By the voter registration deadline: October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 general election (the records are closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election). The Department of Elections says online applications can be submitted through 11:59 p.m. on the final day of registration.

steps.step: Or mail a paper Virginia Voter Registration Application
steps.how: Download the state form VA-NVRA-1, or pick one up at the office or another place the Department of Elections lists (for example DMV offices, public libraries and armed forces recruitment offices). Complete every starred item and sign it. Give your full Social Security number if you have one (the form has a box for 'No SSN was ever issued'): the Department of Elections and the form say an application without an existing number is denied. Phone and email are optional but help the office reach you. Give a mailing address in Box 4 only if your home cannot receive mail, you are homeless, or you are an overseas citizen or a uniformed service member, spouse or dependent; qualifying protected voters (for example law enforcement officers, holders of protective orders and election officials) may give a Virginia P.O. box instead. If your felony conviction is not disqualifying, the Department of Elections says to answer 'yes' to the felony question and 'no' to the restoration question, and that this will not invalidate the application. Mail it to Albemarle County Voter Registration and Elections, 1600 5th Street, Charlottesville, VA 22902, or to the Virginia Department of Elections, 1100 Bank Street, First Floor, Richmond, VA 23219. The federal National Mail Voter Registration Form is also accepted. The form notes that first-time voters who registered by mail must show an acceptable ID (not a written statement) when voting in person in a federal election.
steps.deadline: Postmarked no later than the registration deadline (October 23, 2026 for November 3, 2026). An application with no postmark, or an illegible one, counts if it arrives within five days after the books close (Va. Code § 24.2-416.4(A)). The Department of Elections says one postmarked after the deadline is held and processed after the election.
steps.quote: If mailed, the application must be postmarked no later than the registration deadline.

steps.step: Or apply in person at the registrar's office or another registration office
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration and Elections office; any Virginia general registrar; state-designated voter registration agencies
steps.how: Go to the Voter Registration and Elections office in the County Office Building, 1600 5th Street, Charlottesville (Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.), and fill in the application there. You may also apply at any voter registration office in Virginia. The county office accepts applications for any Virginia locality, and every registrar forwards an application to the registrar where the applicant lives. A state-designated agency such as DMV, social services or an armed forces recruitment office may also take your application by hand; you should get a receipt. If you hand the form to anyone collecting applications, the form's receipt says the collector must submit it within 10 days or by the registration deadline, whichever comes first.
steps.deadline: by the end of the business day when registration closes (October 23, 2026 for November 3, 2026). On that day the office must be open at least eight hours, and people in line at closing may still apply (Va. Code § 24.2-414). The Department of Elections says all registrar offices close at 5:00 p.m. on the final day.

steps.step: Or register or change your address through DMV
steps.who: Applicant; Department of Motor Vehicles; Virginia Department of Elections; General Registrar
steps.how: When you apply for, renew or replace a Virginia driver's license or ID card (not a driver privilege card), or change its address, at DMV in person or online, you are asked whether you are a U.S. citizen and may decline to have your information sent for voter registration. If you say you are a citizen, are 17 or older and do not decline, DMV sends your information to the Department of Elections, which passes it to the Albemarle registrar to accept or reject as a new registration, or as a transfer request if you were already registered and moved within Virginia. Because a DMV address change is treated as a transfer request, a student who gives DMV a parent's address may have the registration moved there.
steps.quote: if the information indicates that the voter has moved within the Commonwealth, the Department of Elections shall transmit the information and the registration record to the appropriate general registrar, who shall treat such transmittal as a request for transfer and process it in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.

steps.step: Military and overseas voters: register with the Federal Post Card Application
steps.who: Active-duty uniformed services members, their spouses and dependents, and citizens living outside the United States
steps.how: Register and request an absentee ballot at the same time on the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA) from the Federal Voting Assistance Program. Mail it, email a scan, or fax it to the Albemarle registrar. With a Virginia DMV license or ID you can also use the Citizen Portal.
steps.deadline: Applications from active-duty uniformed service members, and from spouses or dependents living with them, may be accepted after the books close if, by reason of active duty, they are normally absent from the county (Va. Code § 24.2-419); the exception does not cover other citizens living overseas. The Department of Elections says these FPCAs must still be received by 5:00 p.m. eleven days before the election to get a ballot, except in a qualifying emergency. Overseas citizens who are not military and not yet registered must have the FPCA received by close of business on the final day of registration.
steps.quote: Active-duty uniformed-service voters, their spouses, and their dependents may register to vote or update their voter registration by mail after the final day of registration using the FPCA, an FWAB, or the Voter Registration and Absentee Ballot applications approved by the State Board of Elections.

steps.step: Update your address or name after a move or name change
steps.who: Registered voter; Voter Registration and Elections office
steps.how: Tell a registrar promptly. Use the Citizen Portal (it needs a Virginia DMV driver's license or ID), a DMV address change, a new VA-NVRA-1 form, or a signed letter to the voter registration office for the place you now live. A letter should give your name, enough to identify you (such as your Social Security number), your current and previous addresses, and your signature. State law lets a written name or address notice be sent by mail or fax; whether the Albemarle office takes faxed changes was not confirmed. If you move within Albemarle, the registrar enters the new address, moves you to the new precinct and sends you confirmation. If you move here from another Virginia locality, the request is sent to Albemarle and your record is transferred. If you move here from another state, complete a new Virginia application; it asks where you were registered before. If you miss the deadline after a move within Virginia, state law lets you vote in your old precinct in the next November general election and any election before it, unless your registration has been transferred or cancelled.
steps.deadline: The same as for registering to vote: before the books close (the Department of Elections says postmarked at least 11 days before the next primary or general election). A transfer can be entered only while the records are not closed (Va. Code § 24.2-424(B)).

steps.step: Missed the deadline: register in person on the same day and vote a provisional ballot
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration and Elections office; officers of election; Albemarle County Electoral Board
steps.how: After the books close you can still register, but only in person. During early voting, go to the registrar's office (early voting is in the 5th Street County Office Building, Room A). On Election Day, go to the polling place for the precinct where you live (polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.). You then vote a provisional ballot. The Department of Elections says you are given a notice of the date, time and place where the Electoral Board will decide on it; you may attend but do not have to. For November 3, 2026, early voting runs from September 18 to October 31: weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Saturdays October 24 and 31 from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and Sundays October 18 and 25 from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. A voter already registered in another Virginia locality who is updating may be able to vote a regular ballot instead.
steps.deadline: October 24, 2026 through Election Day (November 3, 2026), per the county; by law, up to and including the day of the election (Va. Code § 24.2-420.1(A)).

steps.step: The registrar decides, then confirms or denies the application
steps.who: General Registrar (Voter Registration and Elections office)
steps.how: The registrar must register every qualified county resident who applies on time and in the required way. You should then get a voter information card or other confirmation (it is not photo ID). If nothing arrives, check the Citizen Portal or contact the office; the Department of Elections suggests doing so if nothing arrives within 30 days. A denial notice must be sent in writing, and by email or phone if you gave them. It comes with a new application and the appeal form.
steps.deadline: A denial notice is due within five days after the denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(A)). No deadline was found for the registrar to decide an application.
steps.quote: Within five days after the denial of an application to register, the general registrar shall notify the applicant of the denial.

steps.step: If denied: correct and resubmit, or appeal to the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.who: Applicant; Voter Registration and Elections office; Clerk of the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.how: You may appeal any denial. If the reason given was a missing signature or a missing required item, you may instead complete and return the new application sent with the denial, or correct it by phone if the office reaches you; a second denial can also be appealed. To appeal, file the Petition for Appeal of Denial of Virginia Voter Registration with the Clerk of the Albemarle Circuit Court, Albemarle County Courthouse, 350 Park Street, Charlottesville. Send the $10 filing fee with it, by check payable to the Clerk of Circuit Court. The court hears it ahead of its other business, and the Commonwealth's Attorney defends. A judgment in your favor entitles you to be registered. The close-of-books rule still applies to a resubmitted application or a petition.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days of being notified of the denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(B))
steps.fee: $10 filing fee for the court petition; no writ tax or security for costs
steps.quote: A person denied registration shall have the right to appeal, without payment of writ tax or giving security for costs, to the circuit court of the county or city in which he offers to register by filing with the clerk of the court, within 10 days of being notified of the denial, a petition in writing to have his right to register determined.

escalation.trigger: Application denied only for a missing signature or a missing required item
escalation.next: Voter Registration and Elections office: return the new application sent with the denial notice, or correct it by phone if the office reaches you
escalation.deadline: Before the registration records close; the close-of-books rule applies to a resubmitted application (Va. Code § 24.2-422(C))
escalation.quote: The general registrar shall advise the applicant that he may complete and submit the new application, in lieu of filing an appeal, if the reason stated for denial is that the applicant has failed to sign the application or failed to provide a required item of information on the application.

escalation.trigger: Registration denied (or a second application denied)
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court, by petition filed with the Clerk; the Commonwealth's Attorney defends and the hearing takes precedence over other business
escalation.deadline: Within 10 days of being notified of the denial
escalation.quote: A person denied registration shall have the right to appeal, without payment of writ tax or giving security for costs, to the circuit court of the county or city in which he offers to register by filing with the clerk of the court, within 10 days of being notified of the denial, a petition in writing to have his right to register determined.

escalation.trigger: The Circuit Court rules against the petitioner
escalation.deadline: Notice of appeal within 30 days from the date of the final judgment order (Va. Code § 8.01-675.3)
escalation.quote: From a judgment rendered against the petitioner, an appeal shall lie to the Court of Appeals.

escalation.trigger: No confirmation and no denial notice received (application apparently not acted on)
escalation.next: Voter Registration and Elections office, then the Virginia Department of Elections
escalation.deadline: A denial notice is due within five days of a denial (Va. Code § 24.2-422(A)); the Department of Elections suggests following up if no acknowledgement arrives within 30 days
escalation.quote: If you believe you have been wrongfully denied registration and have not received any communication, please contact the general registrar for the city or county where you live or the Department of Elections for immediate assistance.

escalation.trigger: Unhappy with how the office handled a registration (delay, lost application, service)
escalation.next: Voter Registration and Elections office first; then the Albemarle County Electoral Board, which appoints the General Registrar (it usually meets on the second Thursday of the month at 9:00 a.m. at the 5th Street County Office Building)
escalation.quote: Localities are primarily responsible for responding to all voter complaints they receive and may request board staff for assistance as needed.

escalation.trigger: Problem not resolved locally, or a time-critical registration problem
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections: informal complaint on the online form or by phone ((800) 552-9745); the online form also notifies the local registrar
escalation.quote: Any person may make an informal complaint electronically or by telephone.

escalation.trigger: A violation of Title III of the Help America Vote Act (which covers the statewide voter registration list and the contents of registration forms)
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections: formal complaint on the notarized ELECT-15512 form mailed to the Deputy Commissioner; hearing on request; alternative dispute resolution if not resolved within 90 days
escalation.deadline: Within 10 days of the incident; final determination within 90 days of receipt of the complaint (Department of Elections)
escalation.quote: A person may file a formal written complaint with the board as required by the Help America Vote Act of 2002, 42 USC § 15301 et seq., using the form and instructions available from the board.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the Commissioner's final determination on a formal complaint
escalation.next: State Board of Elections (it may hold a hearing or rely on the record, and decides within 45 days)
escalation.quote: The Commissioner’s final determination may be appealed to the full State Board of Elections within 15 days.

escalation.trigger: Neglect of a clear ministerial duty, misuse of the office or incompetence by the registrar that has a material adverse effect on the office (for example, applications persistently not processed)
escalation.next: Albemarle County Electoral Board or State Board of Elections. Either may petition the Circuit Court for removal by a recorded majority vote after a public hearing; the Electoral Board may also remove the registrar itself by a unanimous vote after a public hearing (the registrar may appeal to the State Board), and the State Board by a two-thirds vote. A resident can raise the matter with them but cannot file the removal petition: § 24.2-234.1(B) names only the two boards, and the voter-petition route in § 24.2-233 covers elected officers.
escalation.quote: A general registrar may be removed or have removal proceedings instituted against him pursuant to this subsection for (i) neglect of a clear, ministerial duty of the office, misuse of the office, or incompetence in the performance of the duties of the office where such neglect, misuse, or incompetence has a material adverse effect upon the conduct of the office

escalation.trigger: Suspected unlawful conduct under the election laws, such as a false statement on a registration application
escalation.quote: Any complaint or allegation concerning unlawful conduct under this title shall be filed with the attorney for the Commonwealth of the county or city in which the alleged violation occurred.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Dates are for the November 3, 2026 general election only. The County page shows 'Voter Registration Deadline: October 23, 2026' and same-day registration from October 24, which matches Va. Code § 24.2-416(A) as amended in 2025 (records closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election).

Special-election deadlines differ between Department of Elections pages. 'How to Register' gives 14 days before a special election and 7 days before one called by the Governor. 'Registration' gives 11 and 7 days. Under § 24.2-416(A) the records close during the 6 days before a special election called by the Governor, the Speaker, the President pro tempore or a house of the General Assembly, and during the 10 days before any other special election. 'View Your Info' and 'Same Day Voter Registration' still speak of a 21-day period (and a 12-day period for specials), and the latter of an 'October 24 deadline' from an earlier year. This page follows the statute; confirm special-election dates with the office.

Online cut-off: the Department of Elections 'State-designated Voter Registration' page says online applications can be submitted through 11:59 p.m. on the final day of registration. Its 'How to Register' page says all registrar offices close at 5:00 p.m. that day (for in-person and hand-delivered applications). The Citizen Portal itself (vote.elections.virginia.gov) refuses automated readers and is not described here.

Fax and email: the County publishes a fax number (434-972-4178) and lets voters scan and email mail-ballot applications, but its Register to Vote page names only online, mail and in-person registration. The Department of Elections 'View Your Info' page says the change form 'may be faxed', and Va. Code §§ 24.2-423 and 24.2-424(A) allow a written name or address notice by mail or facsimile. Whether the Albemarle office accepts faxed or emailed registration updates was not confirmed. FPCAs may be emailed or faxed (Department of Elections military and overseas page).

Felony convictions: the County's Register to Vote page says a felony conviction must not be for a felony recognized at common law in 1870 and that such a conviction requires restoration of the right to vote; it does not mention a court order. The Department of Elections says that, under a 2026 federal court order, only those felonies take away the right to vote (it lists §§ 18.2-32, 18.2-35 and 18.2-36), and that other felons regain the right to register on release. Va. Code § 24.2-101 as indexed still says no person convicted of a felony is a qualified voter until civil rights are restored. The court order was not read and the legal position may change; applicants should ask the office.

Same-day registration: the provisional ballot comes from the Department of Elections' procedures (§ 24.2-420.1(B)) and its Same Day Voter Registration page. No statute in the index requiring a provisional ballot for same-day registrants was found. The County lists early voting only at the 5th Street County Office Building. That same-day registration is available during all posted early-voting hours is an inference.

Versions: in the index, Va. Code §§ 24.2-101 and 24.2-418 carry contingent expiration or effective-date notes (Acts 2026, cc. 992 and 1081). § 24.2-401 (voting in the old precinct after a move) is marked effective until July 1, 2027, and § 24.2-428 is marked repealed effective July 1, 2027. Re-check these sections after those dates.

Local ordinance: the County Code is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so it has not been checked. The County's Legistar record for matter 25-224 (Board of Supervisors public hearing, 2025-05-07) shows that County Code § 2-101 sets 'Precincts and polling places'; that matter title is the only local text quoted. The section's own text has not been checked. The precinct facts here come from the County's Where to Vote page. No County ordinance on registration itself was found; registration is governed by Title 24.2 and State Board rules.

Fees: no source read (state law, the County pages or the Department of Elections pages) sets or mentions a fee for registering or updating a registration, so none is recorded. No source quote saying registration is free was found. Circuit Court costs beyond the $10 filing fee, and Court of Appeals fees, are not covered here.

The appeal form (f5) is a scanned image with no text layer, overlaid with five fillable text fields (court, city or county, petitioner name, the registrar's city or county, and facts); the signature must still be written by hand. Its fee quote is a transcription from the page image, which a text search cannot confirm. The form says the appeal must be received by the Clerk 'no later than ten days after the date shown on the reverse side'. The PDF has one page and no reverse side; the statute counts 10 days from being notified of the denial.

The VA-NVRA-1 PDF (file name rev-6-2025, footer 'VA-NVRA-1 05/2025') has only a partial text layer, so parts of it, including the rule that mailed applications 'must be postmarked at least 11 days before the next election', are transcriptions from the page images, which a text search cannot confirm. It has no AcroForm or form fields, so 'fillable' is false. The ELECT-15512 PDF declares an AcroForm whose field list is empty and has no widgets, so 'fillable' is false. The FVAP website is a script-built page whose content is not described here; the FPCA link is the www.fvap.gov address the Department of Elections publishes.

Electoral Board: the meeting schedule (second Thursday of the month at 9:00 a.m., more often in the two months before an election) is from the May 2026 capture and may have changed. Whether the Board takes public comment from voters was not found. The Board page lists members with their personal County mailboxes; these are not recorded.

Privacy: the County Elections page names the Director of Elections and General Registrar, the Electoral Board page names its members with personal mailboxes, and the court page names the Clerk and judges. None of these is recorded; only office channels are listed. The mailbox VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org is the one the County's Register to Vote and Elections pages publish for the 'Albemarle County Office of Elections'; its local part splits into the role words 'voter' and 'registration' plus a digit.

City-county line: Charlottesville is a separate independent city with its own General Registrar (see curated/places/va/charlottesville/voter_registration.json). The Charlottesville page warns that the borders are confusing. A home divided by the boundary counts where the bedroom is (1VAC20-40-30(E)). Students living on or near the University of Virginia should check which locality their residence hall or home is in before registering.

Office hours are from the County Elections page (capture of 2026-09-16): Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The How to Vote page lists 'Monday to Friday from September 18 to October 31, 2026' for early voting, although October 31, 2026 is a Saturday that it lists separately. It also gives the building as 1600 5th Street Extended, while the other County pages say 1600 5th Street.

Not confirmed by lexflow's software: the words once quoted for the fee 'Circuit Court petition appealing a registration denial: how to pay (state appeal form)' (https://www.elections.virginia.gov/media/formswarehouse/veris-voter-registration/applications/AppealOfDenialRequest.pdf) were not found on the cited page as lexflow read it (the cited page could not be read (the PDF has no text layer lexflow can read); the form is a scan with no text layer, so a text search cannot read it). Those claims now rest on the cited page as read, without a matched quote; check them at the link before relying on them.

corrections: Quotes: all 77 original structured quotes were confirmed and none was removed. The 56 state-law quotes (legal_basis, steps, fees and escalation) are substrings of I.text_of for their cited sections with whitespace-only normalisation, and each subsection label matches the text. The 11 quotes from official pages (County Register to Vote and Where to Vote, read from the cited Internet Archive captures because www.albemarle.org still returns HTTP 403 with robots.txt included; Department of Elections How to Register, Military & Overseas and Voter Complaints), the 8 from 1VAC20-40-30 and 1VAC20-20-80 (LIS, in legal_basis and escalation) and the Legistar matter title were matched against copies fetched on 2026-10-11. The fee sentence on the scanned appeal form (f5) was re-read from the decoded page image and matches word for word. Four new state-law quotes were added and checked the same way: Va. Code §§ 24.2-416.7(B), 24.2-418(B), 24.2-109(B) (removal by unanimous vote) and 24.2-234.1(B). Quoted fragments in caveats and step text were also checked against their pages; four come from PDF page images (the f5 reverse-side wording, the f1 footer, the f1 postmark rule and 'No SSN was ever issued').

Summary: 'Registration ... closes October 23, 2026' could be read as the books closing that day. It now says October 23 is the last day of regular registration and the records are then closed for the 10 days before the election (Va. Code §§ 24.2-414, 24.2-416(A)). The appeal window now runs from being notified of the denial, as in § 24.2-422(B).

Office name: the County's pages never say 'Department of Voter Registration and Elections'; they say 'Albemarle County Voter Registration and Elections', 'Voter Registration and Elections Office' and 'Office of Elections'. The office field, step 'who' lines, escalation rungs and contact labels now use the County's own name.

s1: the felony rule was stated as settled fact, and the modeller's report said the County page cites a federal court order. It does not: the County page states only the 1870 common-law felony test and the need for restoration for those felonies. The step now attributes the court order, the three listed statutes and the release rule to the Department of Elections, notes that § 24.2-101 as indexed still says otherwise, and attributes the 'not registered in another state' and 'mentally incompetent' items to the County. The residence test now gives both domicile and place of abode (§ 24.2-101). The felony caveat was corrected the same way.

s4: 'call the office to have one mailed' was not supported for the registration form; the County offers to mail vote-by-mail application forms on its How to Vote page. It now says to pick a form up at the office or another place the Department of Elections lists. Added from the form and § 24.2-418(B): the Box 4 mailing-address rule, the protected-voter Virginia P.O. box, the 'No SSN was ever issued' box, the federal-election ID rule for first-time mail registrants, and the Department of Elections' advice on answering the felony and restoration questions.
s5: added the form receipt's rule that an application collector must submit the form within 10 days or by the registration deadline, whichever comes first.

s6: DMV transmits only for a person who says he is a U.S. citizen, is 17 or older and does not decline, and driver privilege cards are excluded (§ 24.2-411.3(A), (C)); the registrar then accepts or rejects (§ 24.2-411.3(D)(1)). The student note was unsourced as a fact; it is now stated as following from a DMV address change being treated as a transfer request (§ 24.2-411.3(D)(2)).

s7: the deadline said active-duty members, spouses and dependents 'may register after the books close'. § 24.2-419 says such an application 'may be accepted' only if, by reason of active duty, they are normally absent from the locality, covers spouses and dependents residing with the member, and does not reach persons temporarily outside the United States (subdivision 3). The deadline now keeps the 'may be accepted', the condition and the limit.

s8: the old-precinct rule now keeps the statute's limit 'unless his registration has been transferred or cancelled' (§ 24.2-401). The Citizen Portal route now notes the DMV credential required by § 24.2-416.7(B) and (C)(2), with a new legal_basis entry for (B). Added that written notices may go by mail or fax under §§ 24.2-423 and 24.2-424(A), with the Albemarle fax practice unconfirmed.

s9: 'You are given a written notice' came from the Same Day Voter Registration page, which says only 'a notice'; the sentence now attributes the notice to the Department of Elections. (The written-notice rule of § 24.2-653(B) is tied to the provisional-voting sections it lists, and no provision applying it to same-day registrants was found.)

s11: 'Otherwise file the Petition' implied that a denial for a missing signature or item could not be appealed. § 24.2-422(A) makes resubmission an option 'in lieu of filing an appeal', and a second denial carries the appeal right; the step now says any denial can be appealed.

Escalation: the no-response rung now also cites the View Your Info page, the source of the 30-day follow-up advice. The removal rung's trigger said 'repeated neglect', which the statute does not require; it now gives the § 24.2-109(B) standard (neglect, misuse or incompetence with a material adverse effect). The rung now adds that the Electoral Board may remove the registrar itself by a unanimous vote after a public hearing (appealable to the State Board) and the State Board by a two-thirds vote, and cites §§ 24.2-234.1(B) and 24.2-233 for the statement that a resident cannot file the removal petition. Legal_basis entries were added for §§ 24.2-109(B) and 24.2-234.1(B).

Forms: f1 'fillable' was null; the PDF has no AcroForm or widgets (including compressed objects), so it is false. f1's title now gives the form's own footer (VA-NVRA-1 05/2025) beside the file name (rev-6-2025). f5 'fillable' was false; the scanned appeal form carries five fillable text fields (court, city or county, petitioner name, registrar's city or county, facts), so it is true and the caveat says so. f6 'fillable' was null; ELECT-15512 declares an AcroForm with an empty field list and no widgets, so it is false.

Caveats: the PDF caveat now records the f1 footer and the 11-day postmark rule read from rendered page images. Checked and left as written: the County Terms and Conditions wording, the special-election deadline conflicts between Department of Elections pages, the 11:59 p.m. online cut-off on the State-designated Voter Registration page, the County's fax number and email ballot-application practice, the archive redirect of /how-do-i/vote to the 2026-08-14 How to Vote capture, the Legistar matter 25-224 title, the Electoral Board schedule, the Charlottesville page's boundary warning, and the version notes on §§ 24.2-101, -401, -418 and -428.

Privacy: re-checked. No staff, Electoral Board member, clerk or judge names are recorded; the only mailboxes are the office mailbox VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org and info@elections.virginia.gov; phone numbers are office main, civil and fax lines. The staff mailbox in the Legistar record's MatterText2 field and the Board members' mailboxes on the Electoral Board page were not recorded.

open_issues: www.albemarle.org still returns HTTP 403 to this client (robots.txt included), so every County fact comes from Internet Archive captures dated 2026-03-17 to 2026-09-16; the live pages were not confirmed.

County Code not read: Municode was not accessed under its terms. The only local text is the Legistar title of matter 25-224 naming County Code § 2-101 (Precincts and polling places); no County ordinance on registration itself was found, and registration is governed by Title 24.2 and State Board rules.

The Citizen Portal on vote.elections.virginia.gov was not read (its robots.txt disallows all automated access), so the online cut-off on the final registration day rests on the Department of Elections' State-designated Voter Registration page.

Felony eligibility is unsettled in the sources: the Department of Elections cites a 2026 federal court order limiting disqualifying felonies, while § 24.2-101 as indexed still requires restoration of rights. The order itself was not read; s1 attributes the rule to the County and the Department and points to the caveat.

Same-day registration: whether the office takes same-day registrations on Sunday November 1 and Monday November 2, after early voting ends, and during every posted early-voting hour, was not confirmed. No statute in the index was found that requires the provisional ballot for same-day registrants; it rests on Department of Elections procedure (§ 24.2-420.1(B)).
Not confirmed: whether the Albemarle office accepts faxed or emailed registration changes.

Special-election deadlines differ between Department of Elections pages (14, 11 and 7 days, and 21 and 12 days on older pages); the caveat gives the statutory periods. The steps cover the November 3, 2026 general election.
Visual-only PDF readings: the f5 fee sentence and reverse-side wording (scanned image), and the f1 footer and postmark rule (partial text layer, read from rendered pages).

No deadline was found for the registrar to decide an application. The Electoral Board's meeting schedule comes from the 2026-05-10 capture, and whether it takes public comment was not found. Circuit Court costs beyond the $10 filing fee and Court of Appeals fees were not researched.
